additional_concerns: For node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909, preservation of existing application processing is converted into a substantive relief exclusion. That is a proposed interpretation, not expressly established by the supplied transition provision. Whether the exclusion persists after a later decision, withdrawal or resubmission remains unresolved.
Node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from its question and executable scope. This narrowing does not establish that those applications are substantively ineligible for relief.

Node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa assesses substantive conditions only; its true result cannot establish actual procedural availability. Node.8eb374ffa546ddd2ba291e37 preserves that unresolved distinction but supplies no executable assessment.

The introductory immediate-effect language and the specific 28 November 2025 commencement provision require contextual reconciliation. The supplied text supports the specific date but does not establish a universal implementation-date test. Node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e should clarify whether its proposed implementation date and assessment_date must coincide.

Additional authority needed to resolve actual procedural availability includes the relevant updated SFC UCITS FAQs and the applicable existing approval or authorisation process. The supplied missing dependency IDs have no identifying metadata permitting a reliable match to those authorities. Which FAQ provisions govern legacy applications and the legally relevant assessment event?

Applying the substantive predicates to an actual change also requires the applicable home-jurisdiction requirements and sufficient grounds for the novelty, complexity and possible local-policy classifications. Those authorities and case facts are not supplied; the formulas expressly leave those judgments unimplemented.

Neither continued post-vetting nor the introductory home-supervision purpose supplies an additional item (ii) eligibility condition. Conversely, removal of prior approval does not itself remove notification, filing or post-vetting obligations.
